# PD subtypes and precision medicine — facts

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Studies in different cohorts report that Parkinson's disease subtypes differ in progression: one reports clusters associated with motor progression rates, another reports faster two-year progression in diffuse-malignant patients, and a third reports that data-driven subtypes exhibited the highest progression rates. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6288789/ · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9937525/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13616926/
- [statement] The SynNeurGe classification of Parkinson's disease proposes three components, pathological α-synuclein, neurodegeneration defined by neuroimaging and pathogenic gene variants, linked to a clinical component; its authors emphasise initial application exclusively for research, and a European Academy of Neurology page lists it among two recent research frameworks for a biological definition of PD. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38267191/ · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine · also: https://www.ean.org/research/resources/neurology-updates/detail/beyond-the-a-synuclein-seed-amplification-assay-shall-we-re-evaluate-the-biological-definition-of-parkinsons-disease
- [statement] In a preprint, the Global Parkinson's Genetics Program authors report that among 65,509 individuals with Parkinson's disease they identified 9,019 (13.8%) potentially trial-eligible genetic variant carriers, including 6,789 GBA1, 2,084 LRRK2, and 146 dual GBA1-LRRK2 carriers. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13119358/ · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine
- [statement] Two analyses of the PPMI cohort by different author groups report that LRRK2-associated Parkinson's disease includes cases negative on the CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay: one reports 46 negative and 102 positive among 148 LRRK2 parkinsonism cases, and another reports SAA-negative patients were markedly enriched for LRRK2 variants. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11925012/ · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13116718/
- [statement] Reports differ on motor progression in SAA-negative Parkinson's disease: an analysis of LRRK2 carriers reports less severe motor manifestations and decline without alpha-synuclein aggregates, while a European Academy of Neurology commentary on a PPMI analysis reports faster time to motor disability milestones in SAA-negative PD, with a relatively small sample. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11925012/ · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine · also: https://www.ean.org/research/resources/neurology-updates/detail/beyond-the-a-synuclein-seed-amplification-assay-shall-we-re-evaluate-the-biological-definition-of-parkinsons-disease
- [statement] The sponsors state that the Phase 2b LUMA study of BIIB122 in early-stage Parkinson's disease did not meet its primary or secondary endpoints (primary endpoint: Time to Confirmed Worsening in the modified MDS-UPDRS Part II and III combined score), and a foundation news article reports that participants treated for at least 48 weeks worsened at a similar rate to placebo. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-22) — https://investors.biogen.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biogen-and-denali-therapeutics-provide-update-phase-2b-luma · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/news-context-parkinsons-drug-luma-lrrk2-clinical-trial-outcomes
- [statement] The sponsors state that LUMA included individuals with early-stage Parkinson's disease with or without a pathogenic LRRK2 variant, and a foundation news article states that the trial largely included patients without known genetic mutations. (medium confidence) — https://investors.biogen.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biogen-and-denali-therapeutics-provide-update-phase-2b-luma · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/news-context-parkinsons-drug-luma-lrrk2-clinical-trial-outcomes
- [statement] After LUMA, Biogen and Denali state they will discontinue further development of BIIB122 in idiopathic Parkinson's disease, while Denali continues the Phase 2a BEACON study in carriers of a pathogenic LRRK2 variant. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-22) — https://investors.biogen.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biogen-and-denali-therapeutics-provide-update-phase-2b-luma · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/news-context-parkinsons-drug-luma-lrrk2-clinical-trial-outcomes
- [statement] The registry record lists the Phase 3 LIGHTHOUSE study of BIIB122 in participants with Parkinson's disease and pathogenic LRRK2 variants as TERMINATED, with the stated reason Sponsor Decision. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-06-26) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT05418673 · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine
- [statement] Authors of two papers link the failure of disease-modifying trials in PD in part to heterogeneity, with one noting that negative trials treated all PD patients as a single homogenous group. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7483040/ · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13616926/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The authors of a PPMI-based analysis report that trial power simulations demonstrated that enrolling DM patients could reduce sample size requirements by approximately 50% using standard trial durations compared to unstratified PD cohorts. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13616926/ · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine
- [statement] In a PPMI analysis, the authors report that the diffuse malignant (DM) subtype had the highest GBA1 frequency, 14.0% versus 5.9% in the mild-motor predominant (MMP) subtype. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13116718/ · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Authors report that replication of published PD subtype classifications is limited: a Delphi-panel replication of eight data-driven systems found none reproducible in LABS-PD, and a separate validation study states that replication studies in independent cohorts are currently lacking. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30056038/ · keywords: PD subtypes and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9937525/
